To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the prevalence of childhood obesity is increasing in most countries, and this increase is due to an energy imbalance between energy intake and expenditure; physical activity levels are decreasing in children; the social, family and built environments are important in promoting physical activity; legislation, policies, and industry are needed to address the issue; and promising physical activity interventions exist.

the current obesity epidemic in children is due to a combination of biological and behavioural factors, including genetic predisposition to obesity, sedentary lifestyles, poor dietary habits, and a lack of physical education in schools, and that the solution to the problem is a combination of individual, community, school, and societal interventions.

the increasing prevalence of obesity in children and youth can be reduced through a comprehensive approach to physical activity that includes: (i) increasing children's participation in physical activity; (ii) decreasing children's sedentary behaviour; (iii) increasing the physical activity of parents; (iv) improving the built, social, and home environments; (v) increasing physical activity opportunities in schools, after-school, and in communities; and (vi) improving physical activity-related public policy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a model for the design and implementation of a physical education program for children and adolescents.
understanding the causes, prevention, and treatment of overweight and obesity, particularly in children.
the development and evaluation of interventions to reduce the prevalence of obesity in children by increasing levels of physical activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evidence supports that children should be encouraged to be more physically active.
physical inactivity and its consequences, including obesity, are major health issues that must be addressed by the international community.
the evidence is compelling that physical activity plays a key role in the development and maintenance of a healthy body composition in children.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
physical activity is an important component of the obesity equation, and that physical activity interventions can have a positive influence on obesity in children.
physical activity and sedentary behaviours are important determinants of obesity in children and youth.
the evidence is clear that physical activity is important for health, and that physical inactivity is a significant contributor to the obesity epidemic.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the obesity epidemic is a serious public health problem that requires a multi-sectorial approach.
we have to do more than simply increase the amount of time that children spend in moderate- to vigorous-intensity physical activity.
we must do more than just tell children to be more active and eat better.
